subject: surgery
title: Urinary stones and obstruction: ESWL, URS and PCNL

steps.tx: **Calcium oxalate stones** are the commonest urinary calculi, while struvite stones form staghorns during infection and uric acid stones remain radiolucent in gout. Cystine stones appear young with hexagonal crystals in the urine. Renal colic radiates from **loin to groin** with haematuria, and non contrast CT confirms the diagnosis while ultrasound suits pregnancy. Infected obstruction above a stone is an emergency needing urgent drainage.
steps.say: Calcium oxalate forms the commonest urinary stone type. Struvite stones form staghorns during urinary infection episodes. Uric acid stones remain invisible on plain films usually. Colic radiates from loin toward groin characteristically. Imaging confirms diagnosis while ultrasound suits pregnancy safely. Infected obstruction needs urgent drainage without delay today.

steps.tx: Both CT panels show a bright **ureteric calculus** obstructing the left collecting system with upstream **hydronephrosis** dilatation above the blockage. The coronal view traces the ureter from the dilated kidney down toward the pelvic stone. The axial view confirms the same stone beside the dilated renal pelvis. Bilateral obstruction or obstruction in a solitary kidney risks **anuria** and needs urgent relief.
steps.say: Both scan panels show a bright obstructing ureteric stone. The kidney above the blockage appears dilated clearly. The coronal view follows the ureter toward the pelvis below. The axial view confirms the stone beside dilated pelvis. Bilateral obstruction risks anuria and needs urgent relief.

vis.caption: CT coronal and axial showing calculus with hydronephrosis. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Medical expulsive therapy** with tamsulosin helps distal ureteric stones between five and ten millimetres to pass spontaneously. Diclofenac provides first line analgesia and metoclopramide controls vomiting during colic episodes. An infected or obstructed kidney needs a **double J stent** or nephrostomy drainage urgently. Shock wave lithotripsy fragments renal stones under two centimetres but pregnancy and coagulopathy contraindicate treatment.
steps.say: Medical expulsive therapy helps small distal stones pass spontaneously. Alpha blockade relaxes the distal ureter during colic episodes. Strong analgesia and antiemetic treatment control symptoms meanwhile. An infected obstructed kidney needs stent drainage urgently. Shock waves break suitable renal stones without surgery afterward. Pregnancy and coagulopathy are contraindications to shock wave treatment.

steps.tx: **Ureteroscopy** with laser dusting and basket retrieval clears most ureteric and renal stones under direct vision. A postoperative stent eases colic while oedema settles after instrumentation. **PCNL** through a percutaneous tract clears stones above two centimetres and complete staghorn burdens effectively. Prone or supine positioning, miniaturised tracts, and tubeless exits suit selected patients, while significant bleeding may need embolisation.
steps.say: Ureteroscopy removes most stones under direct vision safely. Laser energy dusts stones before basket retrieval follows. A stent helps colic while oedema settles afterward. Percutaneous surgery removes large and staghorn burdens effectively. The tract passes through the flank directly to the kidney. Significant bleeding may need embolisation after surgery sometimes.

vis.alt: Diagram comparing Ureteroscopy (URS) for ureteral/renal stones and Percutaneous Nephrolithotomy (PCNL) for larger kidney stones.
vis.caption: URS and PCNL: surgical approaches for urinary stone clearance

steps.tx: Pregnancy needs ultrasound assessment with stent drainage until delivery allows definitive stone treatment safely. Children need low dose imaging and miniaturised instruments scaled to body size throughout. **Stone analysis** after passage guides **metabolic prevention** with high fluid intake above two and a half litres daily. Normal dietary calcium, reduced salt intake, **citrate supplementation**, and allopurinol for uric acid disease reduce recurrence, which still reaches fifty percent at ten years.
steps.say: Pregnancy needs ultrasound assessment before definitive treatment planning. Stent drainage controls obstruction until delivery occurs safely. Children need low dose imaging and miniaturised instruments throughout. Stone analysis guides metabolic prevention after passage occurs. High fluid intake and citrate reduce recurrence risk substantially. Normal dietary calcium protects better than restriction does.
